text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- All sectors, also employees without working contracts, should be included in a broad pay deal which should be all- binding, the white collar union group in the Confederation of Unions for Academic Professionals in Finland (AKAVA) says.
- Obesity may become a new national disease in Finland, whereas fewer Finns die of heart diseases, national health reseachers say.
- The government should take tougher action to limit brothels in Finland, seven MPs urge.
- Neighbourhoods in Helsinki are clearly divided between prosperous west and poor east, a study by the city planning office shows.
- Further studies on economic and monetary union (EMU) requested by parliament will be handled after summer vacations, the government decided on Wednesday.
- Finnish retailer Kesko plans to develop a combination shopping and banking card with banks, company's CEO Eero Kinnunen says.
- Raw wood imports will stay at last's year level even though domestic wood sales are prices are rising, sector representative says.
- Restructuring of European Union's power structures and institutions should be carried on further, Foreign Minister Tarja Halonen says.

- It is time employees got their share of economic growth, says chairman Matti Viitasalo at Confederation of Unions for Academic Professional in Finland (AKAVA), demanding a broad pay deal with a percentage rise in salaries and reduction in taxes.
- Nordic justice ministers agreed to ban active participation in criminal motor cycle groups at their meeting in Norway on Wednesday.
